text: {"score":4,"justification":"The summary is accurate and cautious, and its numbers match the card (8.4%, 3.0%, 5.40, 0.66, 46%, 18 records, 0 of 11). It explains billed level against patient complexity with strata comparisons, flags missing 99215 documentation, and gives a concrete first step. Its weaknesses are a few small misstatements, a generic closing next-step list, and a somewhat muddled sentence.","problems":["The line \"0 of 11 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed had no lab or test line\" is awkwardly worded, and \"the data-reviewed notes all had matching lab or test lines\" slightly overinterprets the card field.","\"roughly double the all-provider rate in the 0-, 1- and 2-condition strata\" is approximately right (0.04 vs 0.02, 0.078 vs 0.034, 0.118 vs 0.053), but the 0-condition stratum is only 4% against 2%, a small absolute difference.","The claim that the \"4-condition stratum actually bills below peers\" is true (0.091 vs 0.123), but it rests on only 44 visits, so it is thin evidence. The summary does not mention the small samples, and it does not note that the 5+ stratum is high at 0.45 vs 0.232.","The high-complexity examples (C0005928, C0006316) are called \"clinically plausible\" without chart support. That is a judgment from the diagnosis lists only.","The next steps are generic and do not name specific claim IDs. The body names the low-complexity claims, but next_steps only says to request a larger sample and re-screen.","The listed example claims are a mixed bag: the C0006003 documentation example is a 99214 and is not about the 99215 issue.","The cited claim C0005128 (diabetes, E11.9) is a weak illustration of excessive coding."]}
